messages:
julia: Heads-up, ACME-EU reported repeated 502s when their traffic goes through their corporate proxy. They have a tiny allowlist (/29) and say their proxy rotates source ports aggressively.

mike: Any edge logs or timestamps? 502s look like our ELB returning upstream resets? :thinking_face:

julia: ELB -> edge pool returning 502s. sample from edge logs:
```
2026-03-16T09:14:22Z 502 GET /v1/generate 10.0.45.12:12345 -> 172.18.6.22:443 conn-reset
```
Customer claims thousands of short-lived outbound connections behind one proxy IP.

ash: Classic SNAT/ephemeral port exhaustion or conntrack churn. If single public IP is opening N concurrent TCP flows and ephemeral ports run out, new connections fail or get reset.

sre-bot: quick-check guidance: run `ss -s` + `ss -tn state time-wait | grep <proxy-ip> -c` and `conntrack -L | grep <proxy-ip> | wc -l` on affected nodes.

mike: LB idle timeout vs proxy keepalive mismatch also common. If proxy closes sockets aggressively, we see many TIME_WAITs and high conntrack churn. Check `net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time` and proxy keepalive settings.

sophia: Customer can't change proxy, only update their allowlist. They only permitted our /29 today. They refuse widening for compliance reasons. What's our recommendation?

darren: Options to propose to them:
- Request they increase allowlist to cover more of our regional egress pool (we can provide a short list of stable ranges).
- Encourage enabling connection pooling/persistent upstream connections on their proxy (reduces ephemeral port usage).
- Short-term: we can offer them a Dedicated egress allocation (deterministic NAT IPs) or Private deployment so their firewall rules map to a fixed set of IPs.

julia: Troubleshooting we ran on the edge nodes:
```
# on affected edge
ss -s
ss -tn state time-wait | awk '{print $1}' | head
sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
```
We observed thousands of TIME_WAIT and conntrack near table limit with many entries tied to the proxy IP.

ash: Quick mitigation we applied (temporary):
- bumped conntrack: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288`
- reduced FIN timeout: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30`
- tuned conntrack hashsize on impacted hosts
Note: these are stopgaps. They increase memory usage and can mask the root cause. Monitoring required.

mike: Commercial workaround idea: pre-allocate a small dedicated egress block for this customer in eu-west-2. That gives deterministic IPs but needs SRE + Sales signoff. I'll check capacity and pricing impact.

sophia: I'll log this in INC-4821 and recommend the following KB steps to the customer:
- capture `ss` / `conntrack` output,
- confirm proxy keepalive/pooling config,
- request larger allowlist OR opt for Dedicated,
- if they refuse wide allowlist, request temporary exceptions during peak windows.

julia: Can someone draft the KB? Keep it short: cause, symptoms, quick checks, internal mitigations, customer actions, and escalation path to Dedicated.

ash: I'll draft the KB and push to eng-infra/docs. Will include commands and a snippet to parse conntrack TTLs.

mike: Action items:
- ash: KB draft + commands (owner)
- julia: attach extracted logs to INC-4821 and request permission to propose larger allowlist (owner)
- mike: evaluate feasibility of dedicated egress block in eu-west-2 and cost/approval path (owner)

sre-bot: monitor: set alert on conntrack_utilization > 75% for edges servicing ACME-EU; 24h watch after any sysctl bump.

julia: We bumped conntrack on a subset of nodes; monitoring shows reduced 502s but memory footprint increased slightly. We'll revert changes if any instabilities occur.

mike: Long-term infra notes: consider adding per-customer SNAT pools (soft carve) and a small-control-plane feature to lease extra ephemeral IPs for high-fanout proxies. Might be product ask for Dedicated/Reserved egress.

sophia: I'll summarize recommendations for the customer in the ticket: 1) allowlist extra IPs we provide 2) enable proxy pooling 3) consider Dedicated if allowlist can't be expanded.

julia: Thanks. Follow up with INC-4821 when customer replies.
